_doc: Why each toggle in `docs/EVAL_STATUS.md`'s `Unreachable by any screen` list is
not a gene. One line each, so the residual count is examined work rather than
an unexamined ceiling. `tools/test_genome_reach_debt.py` requires this file to
cover exactly that computed list: a toggle that becomes reachable must LOSE its
entry here, and a new unreachable toggle must gain one. Neither side can rot.
Groups: `bundle` turns other genes on; `host-only` cannot fire on a native
board; `live-bridge-row` could fire but a gene row would withhold it from the
live bridge; `production-on` ships on and a gene row would switch it off;
`configured-on` ships on from the wrong constructor for the table's own test;
`infrastructure` has no decision content; `already-on` would screen inert.

adjacent_camp_clear.reason: On by default in `BasicAi::new`, so an `enable_*` opt-in row would be on in BOTH arms of every pair and screen as exactly inert — the zero-width failure this repository's fires gate exists to catch. Withholding it is the `legacy()` anchor's route, not an opt-in row.

amenity_districts.reason: Production ships it ON, so its door is `PRODUCTION_TREATMENTS` — and that row is not neutral: `apply_gene_ledger` disables every production treatment whose `ledger_default_on` is `Some(false)`, which is exactly what a screenable tag with no ledger row is. The row would switch a shipped behaviour off at deployment. What it does: the baseline governor may build the district that repairs an Amenity deficit.

bank_envoys.reason: Screenable would mean WITHHELD. It has a `LIVE_TREATMENTS` row, so a `PRODUCTION_OPT_INS` row flips `ledger_default_on` from `None` to `Some(false)` and `apply_gene_ledger` would then take it out of the live bridge. That is a deployment change wearing an instrument's clothes. The move it wants is the door `culture-coverage` went through: out of `FIRAXIS_ONLY_TREATMENTS` and into an `ENGINE_REPAIR_*` half, taken deliberately with the bridge change owned and priced. What it does: the baseline envoy pass must not overwrite a deliberate bank. Its host-only classification is an argument about which rivals the weights were bred against, not a claim the code cannot fire natively.

battlefront_observation.reason: On in `AdvancedAi::configured` but NOT in `promoted_policy_envoy`, so `production_bundle_rows_are_real` rejects a `PRODUCTION_TREATMENTS` row for it as written. Moving the assignment is a controller change owned by whoever owns the behaviour, and it carries the same deployment hazard as the group above. What it does: plan campaigns and battlefronts from player-visible observations only.
